query: How does Postgres detect a deadlock among transactions waiting on each other's locks?

matches.reason: Entry point for the deadlock detector: invoked when a backend has waited too long for a lock, it searches for deadlocks and either signals a fixable soft deadlock (wait-queue reorder) or an unresolvable hard deadlock.
Recursively explores adding soft-edge constraints to the waits-for graph to determine whether a deadlock-free ordering of lock wait queues exists.

The core cycle-detection algorithm: walks the waits-for graph from a blocked process through hard (lock-holder) and soft (queue-order) edges, detecting a cycle back to the start process, which constitutes a deadlock.
